subject.title: Policy plugins cannot see resolved/served model identity at any blocking-capable hook (security impact: our confidentiality guard failed open)

question: Which plugin API surface should become the supported blocking policy point for resolved provider/model identity?
rationale: This touches the public Plugin SDK and a confidentiality enforcement boundary; automation can identify the missing fields, but maintainers need to choose whether the contract is existing hook context, event payload fields, a new post-resolve hook, or broader provider hooks.

options.title: Fill existing hook context
options.body: Populate and document `modelProviderId` and `modelId` consistently for `before_agent_run` across CLI and embedded runners, with focused tests, while deferring raw provider hooks.

options.title: Add a new post-resolve hook
options.body: Create a dedicated pre-call modifying hook with explicit resolved model identity, accepting a broader SDK/API expansion and compatibility review.

options.title: Keep workaround-only policy
options.body: Leave model-based enforcement to configured agent-chain eligibility and telemetry hooks, preserving today’s narrower SDK but not solving per-turn model policy.

recommendation.title: Fill existing hook context
recommendation.body: Populate and document `modelProviderId` and `modelId` consistently for `before_agent_run` across CLI and embedded runners, with focused tests, while deferring raw provider hooks.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the existing blocking lifecycle gate that this issue needs to extend or clarify.
